Added /Applications/Orca.app to neo Dock persistent apps and added AeroSpace rule for com.stablyai.orca to workspace T. nix flake check --no-build and just darwin-switch neo passed; running Orca moved to T.

Root cause: Citrix Viewer was using macOS native fullscreen across displays while macOS had separate Spaces per display enabled, so the right monitor stayed on its own visible AeroSpace workspace. Added system.defaults.spaces.spans-displays = true for neo, applied with just darwin-switch neo, and verified defaults read com.apple.spaces spans-displays returns 1. Full behavioral verification requires logout/login and retesting Citrix.

AeroSpace window detection restored after full reboot. Verified list-windows is populated, permissions are allowed, active config matches repo baseline, and callbacks place visible windows on configured workspaces: Brave/Safari on B and Citrix Viewer on W. Telegram rule remains present for ru.keepcoder.Telegram -> M; needs an open Telegram window for direct verification.
Added Orca on-window-detected rule for com.stablyai.orca -> workspace T, refreshed Home Manager, reloaded AeroSpace, reran callbacks, and verified Orca window is on workspace T.
Cleared recursive com.apple.quarantine from /Applications/Warp.app, verified spctl accepts it as notarized, launched Warp, and confirmed the Warp process is running.

Changed Citrix Viewer rule from tiling to floating while keeping move-node-to-workspace W. Refreshed Home Manager, reloaded AeroSpace, reran callbacks, and verified active config. Existing Citrix windows are macOS native fullscreen, so AeroSpace cannot change their layout live; rule applies to newly created/non-native-fullscreen Citrix windows.

Renamed Raycast script command to Aerospace Toggle, added a local half-normal/half-dark Raycast-derived PNG icon, switched Home Manager, and verified the installed script metadata and icon symlink.

Hardened Raycast AeroSpace Toggle to launch AeroSpace and wait until the server reports a real version before toggling. Applied via Home Manager and tested the installed command twice, leaving AeroSpace enabled.

Replaced blind enable toggle with state-aware logic. When AeroSpace is off, command enables it, reloads config, and reruns on-window-detected callbacks; when already on, it disables. Applied via Home Manager and tested disable->enable, leaving AeroSpace enabled with windows assigned.
